chapters.title: Chapter 5: Reducing Capital Gains Tax Legally

lessons.title: Tax-Loss Harvesting and Using Your Annual LTCG Exemption

body.text: Two simple habits, done before 31 March each year, quietly cut the tax on your portfolio: turn paper losses into real ones that offset gains, and use up your ₹1.25 lakh long-term exemption before it expires.

children.text: Ramesh, a 39-year-old marine engineer in Kochi, realised ₹3,00,000 of long-term gains from redeeming equity mutual fund units in December 2026. He also held a small cap stock sitting on a ₹1,50,000 unrealised loss that he no longer believed in. He planned to sell it "sometime next year". Doing it before 31 March instead saved him ₹18,750.

columns.label: Tax-Loss Harvesting
points: Sell holdings that are in loss before 31 March
The realised loss offsets realised gains, cutting tax this year
Any unused loss carries forward for 8 years if you file on time
Buy back later if you still want the exposure

columns.label: Tax-Gain Harvesting
points: Sell long-term equity holdings in profit, up to ₹1.25 lakh of gain
That gain is exempt, so the tax is nil
Buy back to reset your cost to the higher price
Repeat every year, because the exemption does not carry forward

markDefs.definition: The first ₹1.25 lakh of long-term capital gains on listed equity and equity-oriented funds in a tax year, which is exempt under section 198 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. It is per person per tax year and does not carry forward.

children.text: and this year's realised losses both expire with the tax year. India has no wash sale rule of the kind the US applies, so selling and buying back the same share or fund is not disallowed. What matters is that the trades are genuine, at market prices, on the exchange.

body.caption: Ramesh's year with and without harvesting the ₹1,50,000 loss

body.title: What Harvesting Saved Ramesh
body.prompt: Ramesh has ₹3,00,000 of long-term gains and books a ₹1,50,000 long-term loss before 31 March. Compared with not booking the loss, how much tax does he save, before cess, in rupees?
body.explanation: Without harvesting, taxable gains are ₹3,00,000 − ₹1,25,000 = ₹1,75,000, taxed at ₹21,875. With harvesting, they fall to ₹25,000, taxed at ₹3,125. The saving is ₹18,750, which is simply 12.5% of the ₹1,50,000 loss.

body.label: The Harvesting Formula
body.context: For long-term equity gains above the exemption, every rupee of long-term loss you realise saves 12.5 paise of tax. Against 20% short-term gains, a short-term loss saves 20 paise per rupee.

children.text: Gain Harvesting: Use the Exemption or Lose It

The ₹1,25,000 exemption resets every 1 April. If your long-term equity gains for the year are below it, you are leaving tax-free room unused. Meera, a 34-year-old architect, holds an index fund whose long-term gain grows by about ₹1,25,000 a year. If she redeems and reinvests that much every year, each redemption is inside the exemption and is taxed at nil, and her cost resets higher each time.

body.title: Tax on ₹6,25,000 of Gains Built Over 5 Years

children.text: Selling the whole holding in one year gives a ₹6,25,000 gain, of which only ₹1,25,000 is exempt, so ₹5,00,000 is taxed at 12.5%: ₹62,500. Harvesting ₹1,25,000 a year uses five separate exemptions and pays nothing. The gain is the same; only the timing changed.

body.title: Use It or Lose It
body.textWithBlank: Any part of the ₹1.25 lakh annual exemption you do not use in a tax year ___, because it cannot be carried forward.
body.explanation: The exemption is per person per tax year. On 1 April it resets to ₹1.25 lakh again, whatever you did or did not use last year.

body.title: The Same-Day Trap
body.question: Ramesh sells 500 shares from his demat account to book a loss and buys the same 500 shares back a few hours later the same day, in the same account. What is the risk?
options: None, this is the standard way to harvest losses
The round trip can be treated as an intraday trade, making it speculative business income rather than a capital loss
The loss is disallowed under India's wash sale rule
He must pay double STT on the buy leg
body.explanation: India has no wash sale rule, so buying back is allowed. But a same-day sell and buy in the same account can be squared off as an intraday position, which is speculative business income, not the capital loss he wanted. Selling for delivery and buying back the next trading day keeps the record clean.

body.text: Harvesting is not free. A round trip costs brokerage, STT on both legs for shares, stamp duty, exchange and GST charges, and it exposes you to an overnight price move. On a ₹5,00,000 equity harvest, STT and stamp duty alone come to roughly ₹1,075. If the stock gaps up before you buy back, that can cost more than the tax you saved.

children.text: Costs differ by asset. On shares, STT is 0.1% on each leg of a delivery trade, so a ₹5,00,000 round trip carries about ₹500 on the sale and ₹500 on the purchase, plus roughly ₹75 of stamp duty on the buy. Equity mutual fund redemptions carry a much smaller STT and no STT on the fresh purchase, but can carry exit load.

FIFO matters. When you buy back units or shares, the new lot goes to the back of the queue. Your oldest remaining units are still the first to be redeemed next time, so check your lot dates before you assume the next sale is long-term.

Some holdings cannot be harvested. ELSS units are locked in for three years from each instalment, and funds with an exit load may charge you for redeeming early. Never harvest a holding you would not otherwise be willing to sell and rebuy.
Leave time for settlement and for the tax year end. Trades must be completed before the market closes for the financial year, so plan a few days before 31 March rather than on the last day.

body.title: Harvesting Against a Property Gain
body.scenario: Sunita sold a plot in tax year 2026-27 and has a long-term capital gain of ₹9,00,000 after indexation choices. She also holds equity shares carrying an unrealised long-term loss of ₹2,00,000 that she is happy to exit.
body.prompt: Can her equity loss reduce the tax on her property gain, and what would it save?
body.modelAnswer: Yes. A long-term capital loss can be set off against any long-term capital gain, whatever asset it came from, so her equity loss can reduce the property gain. Without harvesting, tax is 12.5% of ₹9,00,000 = ₹1,12,500. After booking the ₹2,00,000 loss, the taxable gain falls to ₹7,00,000 and tax to ₹87,500, a saving of ₹25,000 before cess. Note that the ₹1.25 lakh exemption does not apply to property gains, and she must complete the equity sale within the same tax year as the property sale.

stats.label: Deadline
stats.context: Both losses and the annual exemption belong to the tax year

stats.label: Exemption
stats.context: Per person per tax year, not per family or per account

stats.label: Wash sale rule
stats.context: Buying back is allowed, but avoid same-day round trips

stats.label: Round-trip cost
stats.context: STT and stamp duty on a ₹5 lakh equity harvest

body.text: Every individual has their own ₹1.25 lakh exemption. An adult family member investing from their own funds and reporting the gains in their own return uses their own exemption. Shifting your own money into someone else's name to multiply exemptions raises clubbing and ownership questions, so keep funding and ownership genuine.

cards.definition: Booking unrealised losses before 31 March so they offset realised gains.
Booking long-term equity gains up to ₹1.25 lakh so they are exempt, then reinvesting.
Buying back after harvesting a gain gives you a higher cost for future sales.
A US rule disallowing losses on quick repurchase. India has no equivalent.
Selling and rebuying the same scrip on one day can be treated as intraday, which is speculative income.
STT, stamp duty, brokerage, GST and price risk incurred to harvest.

body.title: Your February and March Routine
steps: List realised gains and losses so far this tax year from broker and fund house statements
List unrealised losses you would be willing to book, and check holding periods for each
Book enough losses to offset the gains you want to shelter, keeping the ₹1.25 lakh exemption in mind
If your long-term gains are below ₹1.25 lakh, harvest gains up to the limit and reinvest
Sell for delivery and buy back on a later trading day, not the same day
Complete all trades a few days before 31 March and keep the contract notes

points: Realised losses and the ₹1.25 lakh exemption both expire at the end of the tax year
Booking a long-term loss saves 12.5% of that loss; a short-term loss against short-term gains saves 20%
Gain harvesting resets your cost higher at zero tax when gains are within the annual exemption
India has no wash sale rule, but avoid selling and rebuying the same scrip on the same day
Long-term equity losses can shelter long-term gains from any asset, including property
Count the round-trip costs and price risk, and never harvest a holding you would not willingly sell

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax or investment advice. Figures are illustrative and ignore brokerage, surcharge and cess unless stated. Sections and rates reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 for tax year 2026-27. Do not let tax planning override your investment judgement, and consult a qualified tax professional before acting.
